title: Parabolic semi-regular duality and the reverse-column label map
statement: Assume AC. For the reversed-block standard parabolic $\bar p\subset gl_n$, grade simple Levi roots by0 and outside roots by1, so $g_0=\bar l$, $g_{<0}=\bar u^-$ and $\gamma=2\rho_g-2\rho_{\bar l}$ is a Levi character. There is the explicit semi-regular $U(g)$-bimodule $S_{\bar u,\gamma}=U(\bar u^-)^\#\otimes U(\bar p)$, with the two PBW module identifications. Tensor/Hom give inverse exact equivalences on finite-rank graded free/cofree $U(\bar u^-)$ objects. Restricted contragredient dual and $c(X)=-w_0X^tw_0$ give an exact CONTRAVARIANT equivalence $\Psi$ from finite generalized-standard flags for $\bar p$ to those for $p$. The Levi highest-weight map is $\lambda_{\bar A}\mapsto-w_{\bar J}\lambda_{\bar A}-2\rho_{\bar u}$, then $-w_0$; in reverse/original column readings it gives $a_i+i-1$, so $\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A)$. BGG restricted duality $D$ gives the COVARIANT equivalence $F=D\Psi$ from opposite standard flags to target costandard flags, with $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$. It preserves the corresponding central blocks and reverses the label order. These are exact filtered-category assertions, not equivalences on all objects of category O and not the unchanged underived full-longest Borel twisting functor.
strategy: Use the outside-root grading and finite-Levi PBW slices from15. The character identity gamma([X,Y])=tr_l(adX adY) follows by Levi invariance, checking outside simple e_alpha against f_alpha with the root/sl2 trace calculation; other weights give0. Construct right action via N# tensor_N U and left action via Hom_B(U,C_gamma tensor B). For H in l, H(f tensor1)=−(f adH)tensor1+f tensor(H+gamma(H)); for X in g1 decompose nX=Xn+sum H_i H_i^X(n)+F_X(n), giving X(f tensor1)=f tensorX+sum(fH_i^X)tensor(H_i+gamma(H_i))+(fF_X)tensor1. Commutation with right g−1 reduces to the displayed trace identity, and generation by g0,g±1 proves bimodule commutation. The left PBW map is triangular for positive Levi-radical degree followed by Levi PBW degree: leading f tensor b and strictly lower corrections prove surjectivity and injectivity by finite induction, avoiding the source's false finite-dimensional degree-zero comparison. The adjoint unit/counit reduce to graded free/cofree evaluation and End_N(N#)=N^op, so no completion is hidden. On an induced finite Levi simple E, the dual top space is C_−gamma tensor E*, hence the stated standard transport; induction restricts both functors to finite flags. Ungraded transfer uses zeta eigenvalue classes moduloZ and restricted weight duals. In a target column of lengthr and offsetb the reverse source offset isb'=n−b−r; w0w_Jbar preserves within-column position and 2w0rho_ubar=b−b'. Thus transformed component a_i+(b'+k−1)+(b−b')=a_i+i−1. This proves the exact label and scalar central shift. D then changes variance and standards to costandards. The source free/cofree and flag hypotheses are checked here, not presumed for arbitrary O.

title: Residue Casimir operators and local affine-Hecke actions
statement: Assume AC and work with finite $n$ classical $gl_n$ category O, distinct from the Fock algebra $gl_{I^+}$. Tensor Casimir $x_j$ on the jth natural factor (including all preceding factors) and adjacent place swaps $T_j$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$ satisfy the degenerate affine-Hecke relations: commuting $x_j$, symmetric-group braid/quadratic relations, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$ and commuting distant generators. They restrict naturally to repeated residue functors $f_i^r$, where $x_j-i$ is locally nilpotent; dual actions are biadjoint mates on $e_i^r$. Finite Levi tensor decomposition and exact PBW induction give multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags for the entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. The standard-class map $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ gives the full integral Fock K0 action, its Chevalley/Serre relations and local integrability; each root's biadjoint functors therefore give a positive, locally finite $sl_2$ action on the simple-class basis. The ground-state class generates the highest constituent, not generally the entire tensor Fock module.
strategy: The natural tensor Casimir is sum E_ab tensor E_ba, and x_j adds the place transpositions with earlier natural factors. Matrix-unit multiplication proves x commutation and T_jx_jT_j=x_{j+1}−T_j, hence the listed relations, with braid and distant commutation immediate on places. For highest weight lambda_j=a_j+j−1, c(lambda)=sum lambda_j(lambda_j+n+1−2j), c(V)=n; the eigenvalue on the lambda+epsilon_j flag factor is (c(lambda+epsilon_j)−c(lambda)−n)/2=lambda_j+1−j=a_j. On lambda−epsilon_j in tensor V* it is −a_j−n+1; an entry i+1 therefore gives −n−i. Exact generalized eigenspaces select precisely the moves. Tensor identity plus finite Levi complete reducibility produces each valid column move once; projected invalid/repeated-column moves disappear. Standard and simple K0 bases and character injectivity were proved in15, so the standard-class map is an actual isomorphism and the induced generators are the explicit tensor/wedge action. Checking on this basis proves Chevalley and Serre relations, including the integral divided powers. Each residue root is locally finite because the fixed finite boxes have only two relevant entries and repeated replacements terminate. Biadjunction, finite length and positivity in the simple basis make class vanishing equivalent to functor vanishing, satisfying every weak-sl2 hypothesis without a forward reference to the later combined action theorem. Restrict x to the chosen generalized eigenfunctor; nilpotence follows on finite flags, hence on finite length. Define the dual x/T by mates, which preserves the relations and both adjunctions.

title: The local affine-Hecke socle argument for residue translations
statement: Assume AC and the preceding positive biadjoint residue $sl_2$/local degenerate affine-Hecke action. At a coincident eigenvalue the completed affine-Hecke algebra on r steps is $Mat_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre. The first-i image in its central fibre is $Mat_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where $Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\ldots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\ldots,h_r)$ is a finite local complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom ri$ and one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent restriction have the corresponding simple head/socle. Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either0 or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$, respectively. Vanishing is exactly absence of that crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation crystal claim, not only its K0 action.
strategy: Use polynomial representation T_j=s_j−partial_j, partial_j=(1−s_j)/(x_j−x_{j+1}); PBW follows by ordered spanning and leading permutation independence after localization. At the coincident completion, partial_j=(x_j−x_{j+1}+1)^−1(1−T_j), with LEFT inverse. Polynomial multiplication and longest divided difference give the relative perfect trace; reduction is the actual coinvariant Frobenius pairing, and complete-local Nakayama gives every matrix unit. The trivial/sign symmetric-group idempotents have fibre rank1: divided-difference terms lower degree and the diagonal character is the regular coinvariant character; idempotent splitting and Nakayama lift rank1. Partial elimination of remaining elementary coefficients gives the displayed h-relations. Their only common zero is0, since vanishing of i consecutive h's and their recurrence makes the reciprocal elementary series polynomial, hence constant. Nullstellensatz makes the quotient finite; polynomial Cohen–Macaulayness and the actual system-of-parameters theorem give regularity, globally by homogeneous localization. Koszul Hilbert series yields dimension binomial(r,i); the variable and h Koszul resolutions compute a unique socle in degree i(r−i). Thus no Grassmannian/Poincare theorem is imported. The ordered partial ring is free of rank i! over this centre and has dimension r!/(r−i)!, by successive monic distinguished-root equations. PBW group cosets and this basis prove the restriction freeness; the complementary idempotent removes (r−i)! multiplicity and leaves the indecomposable projective over Mat_{i!}(Z), with simple head/socle. These are the full algebraic steps of CR3.2–3.3/3.6. In the positive simple-class basis the sl2 string-height filtration is stable; biadjunction prevents a socle/head summand of E^jS from having lower maximal string height than S. At an extremal simple FS=0, E^(r)S is a single opposite-extremal simple by finite sl2 string theory/positivity. The Hecke action on E^rS has multiplicity module K_r; complementary restriction forces the socle/head of E^(j)S simple, since no maximal-height summand is killed by E^(r−j). Dimension comparison gives binomial(r,j) leading multiplicity and smaller-height other factors. For a general S take an extremal quotient of F^(h_minus)S and use adjunction to embed S in its divided translate; the opposite extremal translate is a sum of one simple, and the adjoint Hom into its simple socle bounds its multiplicity by1. This proves CR5.20 without importing it as a black box. Source Fock L is the balanced SOURCE upper-chart family. Kashiwara93§5.1 proves kernels of powers spanned by the global vectors with bounded epsilon (apply the maximal string power and balanced injectivity); §5.2 finite sl2 highest-string filtration is balanced by isolating a maximal constituent and annihilator test, whose remainder lies in the zero triple intersection. Thus in each associated string fG=[phi]G(tilde f) and eG=[epsilon]G(tilde e), and all other constituents have smaller corresponding height. The actual upper/lower string definitions in§3, the two source-positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing verify these hypotheses; this is not the library8 adjoint-bar family by fiat. The full source5.3.1 proof uses the upper divided-string expansion and kernel-spanning induction to lift that leading term. At1, comparing with the preceding categorical unique maximal-height factors gives precisely the stated tableau labels. Commuting restricted duality makes head and socle equal and gives self-duality; one simple socle forces indecomposability.
